title: Control plane domain matrix and runtime-adapter notes (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft that defines service domain boundaries in the control plane, the routing policy decision matrix for multi-region and multi-tier traffic, and a first-pass mapping of runtime adapter responsibilities. Goal: make clear which subsystem owns what (API Gateway, Orchestrator, Runtime Adapters, Model Registry, Telemetry, Autoscaler), and capture routing policy primitives we can compose for canarying, cost-aware routing, and region failover.

Context and constraints (short):
- We need deterministic routing behavior for PLG hosted API customers, plus flexibility for Dedicated/Private customers to plug in custom routing.
- Latency SLOs vary by plan; control plane must enforce SLO-aware routing (i.e., prefer low-latency region but degrade to cost-fallback when underutilized).
- Runtime adapters hide pool-specific details (GPU type, quantization flavor, KV cache compatibility). Serving-runtime team implements adapters; platform-engineering owns adapter registry and policies.
- Target infra: k8s for control plane services, mixed cloud regions (us-west1, us-east4, eu-west1), and on-prem/AZ islands for Private installs.

High level domain responsibilities (intent, not exhaustive):
- Edge/API Gateway (owned: eng-platform-ingress)
  - Auth, per-tenant rate limiting, ingress shaping, initial routing decision (map request -> routing domain)
  - Short-circuit simple policy checks (blocked tenant, embargoed model)
  - Exposes routing hints downstream via X-Redwood-Routing header

- Routing & Policy Service (owned: platform-engineering)
  - Central policy evaluation: cost/latency/affinity rules, A/B and canary configs, region preferences
  - Produces route plan: sequence of candidate runtime endpoints, fallbacks, TTL for selection
  - Maintains feature flags and rollout windows (integrates with LaunchDarkly / in-house flag service)

- Control Plane Orchestrator (owned: platform-engineering)
  - Request-level orchestration for complex flows (function calls, tools, multi-model fanout)
  - Model version pinning and rollout coordination (canary -> linear rollout)
  - Coordinate KV cache metadata and sticky cache affinity when applicable
  - Exposes Admin APIs for emergency cutovers and manual overrides

- Runtime Adapter Registry (owned: platform-engineering, runtime impl by serving-runtime)
  - Canonical list of adapter types and capabilities: fast-gemm-k8s, triton-v100, quant-llama-q4, cpu-embeddings, onprem-hsm
  - Adapter capability schema (string list): supported-sequence-length, kv-cache, streaming, quantization-profile
  - Adapter versioning: adapters are semver; orchestrator uses compatibility matrix to select safe fallbacks

- Runtime Pools (owned: serving-runtime & infra)
  - Physical workers that take routed work. Responsibility split: infra owns cluster lifecycle; serving-runtime owns runtime binary and kernel selection configs.

- Autoscaler & Capacity Manager (owned: eng-platform-autoscale)
  - Tracks pool utilization, issues scale commands, predicts capacity needs for rolling model updates

- Telemetry/Tracing/Cost (cross-cutting: observability team)
  - Token-level cost attribution, per-request latency histograms, and error categorization; used by routing policy for cost-aware decisions

Routing policy primitives (to be implemented by Routing & Policy Service):
1) region_preference: ordered list of regions by latency/cost for tenant/model
2) cost_fallback_threshold: if cost delta > X% route to cheaper region unless latency breaches SLO
3) sticky_cache_affinity: keep requests for same tenant/model on same pool for TTL to improve KV cache hit rate
4) canary_ratio: percent of traffic to new model variant; supports header-based and cookie-based population selectors
5) geo_blocking: block/allow lists per tenant (for regulatory requirements)
6) capacity_fallback: route to lower-tier model variant when preferred pool signals capacity_pressure
7) prewarm_hint: orchestrator can request prewarm on specific pool before rollout window

Example flow (short):
- Client -> API Gateway validates JWT and looks up tenant profile -> adds X-Redwood-Tenant and X-Redwood-Routing-Hint (if any)
- Gateway calls Routing Service (lightweight call) -> receives route plan: [us-west1/pool-A (primary), us-east4/pool-B (fallback), eu-west1/pool-C (regulatory-only)] plus token for TTL
- Gateway forwards to chosen runtime endpoint or to Orchestrator for multi-model orchestration

Multi-region failover behavior (policy):
- Soft failover: if primary latency > SLO for 10s window AND secondaries healthy, start draining new requests to fallback gradually (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
- Hard failover: explicit region outage -> immediate switch to fallback with confirmation step recorded in audit logs
- Regulatory hold: if regulatory constraint requires data residency, region selection filtered prior to cost/latency logic

Runtime adapter responsibilities (delineation):
- Platform-engineering adapter registry: provides capability schema and selection logic; exposes adapter health/status to orchestrator
- Serving-runtime adapter implementation: the binary/library that exposes the adapter API (load_model, infer, stream, health_check, cache_invalidate)
- Adapter contract (required endpoints): /health, /capabilities, /load, /infer, /invalidate-cache, /metrics
- Compatibility guarantees: serving-runtime ensures adapter complies with contract for declared semver; platform config must defend against incompatible adapter by only routing to adapters whose capabilities match request requirements

Ownership matrix (one-line rows):
- API Gateway: auth, rate-limit, header propagation, initial routing hint generation -> owner: eng-platform-ingress
- Routing & Policy Service: policy evaluation, route plan generation, A/B, canary, failover logic -> owner: platform-engineering
- Orchestrator: multi-model flows, rollouts, KV affinity, admin overrides -> owner: platform-engineering
- Runtime Adapter Registry: capability schema + registry & selector -> owner: platform-engineering
- Runtime Adapters: adapter binaries, model loading, per-inference optimizations -> owner: serving-runtime
- Runtime Pools / infra: cluster lifecycle, pool autoscaling primitives -> owner: infra-team
- Telemetry & Cost backplane: token-level attribution, raw traces -> owner: observability-team

Open questions / known TODOs (actionable):
- TTL semantics for route plans: what is safe TTL when KV cache affinity required? (action: spike to measure cache-warmup time; owner: Marco)
- How do we express mixed constraints: e.g., a tenant requiring EU residency but with latency SLO that prefers US region? Needs a policy precedence model. (owner: Priya)
- Can we standardize the adapter capability schema (minimal viable set) before next release? (owner: serving-runtime -> Leah)
- Implement simulation harness for cost-aware routing to estimate monthly cost delta for representative workloads (owner: platform-eng-sre)

Operational notes and emergency playbook snippets:
- Emergency model rollback: orchestrator exposes /admin/rollback/{model_id}; rollback triggers immediate model unload and route re-evaluation; audit event captured in event-store
- Partial region outage: mark region status degraded in Routing Service; notify infra pager and toggle slow-failover policy for 2 hours

References and related tickets:
- Linear: PLT-482 runtime adapter schema (linked above)
- GH: infra PR 912 - initial adapter registry schema (linked above)
- Confluence: (TBD) control-plane runbook page - will link when created

Appendix — small decision log (why this split):
- Why keep adapter registry in platform-engineering? Because selection policy is tightly coupled to routing logic and rollout semantics; registry must evolve with policy changes.
- Why serving-runtime own adapter implementations? They need tight control over kernel selection and performance regressions; also they run the heavy CI/PBench tests.

Next steps (next 2 sprints):
- Finalize adapter capability schema v0.1 and publish JSON Schema (owner: Leah)
- Implement route-plan TTL and soft-failover prototype in staging (owner: Marco)
- Run 2-week simulation for cost-aware routing on sampled traffic (owner: Priya)

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratch):
- Consider adding a "regional affinity score" that blends latency, KV cache hit-rate, and estimated cost to compute a single routing score
- Potential long-term: let Dedicated customers opt into "control-plane-lite" where orchestration decisions are local to their VPC for compliance

(END OF DRAFT)
